correctness.rationale: For every finite a,b,epsilon, a monotone coupling of greedy and arbitrary competing visited-count chains proves all-horizon cover-time dominance. Under greedy control, independent odd/even arrival clocks yield the stated exact maximum of independent geometric sums. For fixed epsilon in (0,1), the geometric triangular arrays have bounded third centered moments and Riemann-sum mean/variance coefficients I and V, giving the independent Gaussian maximum and final-part probability by continuous mapping. Second-moment uniform integrability yields the mean correction, and Chebyshev proves sharpness outside the window. An executable standard-library checker supplies 6250 exact finite rational tests; finite tests are not presented as the proof.

evidence: In the exact model the discovery probability when j of m vertices are unseen is epsilon+(1-epsilon)j/m. In the distinct two-offer choice walk it is 1-(1-j/m)^2.
The full 2020 controlled-walk paper defines exactly the epsilon model but its explicit cover-time results are graph-general bounds, not the geometric maximum or Gaussian terminal-class law.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A two-offer walk cannot be substituted by choosing an effective constant epsilon: its quadratic state dependence differs from the affine dependence here. A general coupon-clock CLT alone does not identify the precise controlled graph process, its globally optimal strategy, or the coupled terminal-part law.

Primary full texts give broad graph cover bounds, not the exact finite law or this asymptotic. value.rationale: The exact cover-time law is a natural nontrivial controlled random-walk observable for arbitrary bipartite part sizes. Its normal maximum and square-root imbalance transition quantify a new second-order phenomenon under fixed positive controller access, sharply contrasting with the coupon-collector extremes of the uncontrolled walk. The combined exact stochastic optimality, distribution and phase crossover carry information unavailable from first-order general graph bounds; not a selected small-parameter computation.
